metadata.source_prompt: Build me a movie-accurate wearable Iron Man Mark 43 suit from Age of Ultron with all the small polygon armour plates that open and close, repulsors, a HUD and an IMU. Budget $60000

design.summary: Iron Man Mark 43 (full wearable suit): 350 printed pieces, 7.7 kg filament, motorised faceplate, $327 incl. filament

uses: LM2596 set to 5 V for the faceplate servos
second LM2596 set to 5 V for the LED rings
webbing straps closing the shells round each limb
rail splices, the star ground and bus hubs

assumptions: armour shape from: suit: designed directly by scripts/forge_mark43.py from reference photos of the movie suit; 3 mm walls, 2 mm faceplate, 15 % gyroid infill (shells are mostly walls)
the suit is worn armour over a black undersuit: the wearer moves every joint; nothing powers the limbs (hobby servos cannot move a person)
the wearer is an average adult male body at 1.75 m and the pieces scale evenly with height; check against your own measurements before printing
gaps at the groin, armpits and elbows are cut on purpose so the joints move; the undersuit shows through them, as on real builds
cable channels are 7 to 10 mm deep on the inside of the shells: there is no body model, so their room against a real wearer is not checked; fit the suit before bonding them

notes: No cable shows from outside: every lead leaves the compartment through its floor, through a port in the back shell, and lies in the channels bonded inside the shells. Press the wires in one at a time past the snap lips.
Set both LM2596 outputs to 5.0 V with a meter before wiring anything to them.
The cells have no protection board: charge them out of the suit at 4.2 V per cell, and stop at 3.2 V per cell (6.4 V at the pack): the regulators fall out of 5 V at about that point.
The Nano runs from VIN, so USB and the pack can be connected together.
Eye LEDs hang on D3 and D5 through the 100 ohm resistor of the part: 20 mA each is an AVR pin's stated limit, so run them under full PWM for long stretches.

WS2812 data: fit a 330 ohm resistor in series at the Nano pin of each ring and a 1000 uF capacitor across 5 V and GND at each ring. The run to a palm is over a metre of unscreened data: test it on the bench before closing the shells.
All three rings at full white load their LM2596 past its 2 A continuous rating (2.16 A; 3 A peak): limit brightness to 90 % in the sketch for anything longer than a burst.
Run time from the 2.5 Ah pack at the typical 1.062 A: about 1.9 h, keeping 20 % back (estimate; lights and faceplate never all run like that for hours).
